newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shekel lower against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israel shekel lower against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies on Tuesday following the rise of the U.S. currency on overseas markets, dealers said.
"The day started with a sharp decline of the shekel following the dollar's rise abroad," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
The dollar rose against the mark in Europe on Tuesday after Germany's Bundesbank left its repurchase rate unchanged.
The dealer said that when the shekel reached 3.535 shekels per dollar investors started selling dollars.
"It seems that the shekel is stablising at a range of 3.52-3.535 shekels per dollar," she said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5320 shekels compared with 3.5220 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7688 against 3.7666 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9887 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9864 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.9247 shekels compared with 1.9365 on Monday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5300 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x238 DMG TCC
